cards.back: Driving is a privilege rather than a right, and the MVA may place restrictions on your license to keep your driving safe.
cards.front: Is driving a right or a privilege?

cards.back: A restriction limits your driving privileges and can come from your license type or from breaking motor vehicle laws; driving against a restriction is a serious offense that can cost you your privileges.
cards.front: Is driving against a license restriction a minor matter?

cards.back: Seat belt, passenger, nighttime and wireless device restrictions apply to graduated license holders under eighteen.
cards.front: Which restrictions apply to graduated license holders under eighteen?

cards.back: A Provisional License holder must always wear a seat belt, and every passenger must use a seat belt or child safety seat.
cards.front: Who must buckle up when a Provisional License holder drives?

cards.back: Provisional License and Learner's Permit holders may not use any wireless communication device while driving, hands-free included, except to call nine hundred eleven in an emergency.
cards.front: May a permit or provisional holder use a hands-free phone while driving?

decks.module: driving as a privilege and what restrictions are; wireless device and seat belt restrictions

cards.back: A provisional driver under eighteen may not drive unsupervised with passengers under eighteen for the first one hundred fifty-one days, unless the passengers are immediate family.
cards.front: For how long may a provisional driver under eighteen not drive unsupervised with passengers under eighteen?

cards.back: During that period an unrelated passenger under eighteen may ride along only when a qualified supervising driver is also in the vehicle.
cards.front: During that period, when may an unrelated passenger under eighteen ride along?

cards.back: Immediate family for the passenger rule means a spouse, child, stepchild, sibling or stepsibling, or any relative living at your address.
cards.front: Who counts as immediate family for the passenger rule?

cards.back: A Provisional License holder may drive unsupervised from twelve midnight to five a.m. only when going to, from or during a job.
cards.front: Between which hours is unsupervised provisional driving limited to exceptions such as work?

cards.back: The other nighttime exceptions are trips to or from an organized volunteer program, an official school activity, or an athletic event or training session you take part in.
cards.front: Which of these is a nighttime exception for provisional drivers?

cards.back: The passenger restriction is limited to the first one hundred fifty-one days, but the midnight to five a.m. rule allows unsupervised driving only for work, volunteer, school or athletic trips.
cards.front: How do the passenger and nighttime restrictions differ in length and exceptions?
cards.memory_hook: Days for riders, trips at night

decks.module: the provisional passenger restriction; the midnight to five nighttime restriction

cards.back: By driving or trying to drive on a road or on private property open to the public in Maryland, you agree to take a drug or alcohol test when an officer asks.
cards.front: What does driving on a Maryland road mean you have agreed to?

cards.back: If an officer has reason to think you are impaired by drugs, alcohol or a controlled substance, a drug recognition expert may ask you to submit to a blood test.
cards.front: Who may ask you to submit to a blood test when impairment is suspected?

cards.back: Your license will be suspended if a test shows a blood alcohol concentration of point zero eight percent or more.
cards.front: At what test result will your license be suspended for alcohol?

cards.back: Drug impairment counts too: having drugs in your system that impair you leads the MVA to suspend your license.
cards.front: Can drug impairment also lead to a license suspension?

cards.back: Refusing a test also costs you: once an officer certifies in writing that you refused, the MVA suspends your license.
cards.front: What happens if an officer certifies in writing that you refused a test?

cards.back: Trying to obtain a fake identification card, permit or driver's license can bring fines, prison or both under federal and state law.
cards.front: What can trying to obtain a fake ID or license bring?

cards.back: Lying about your age to buy, possess or get alcohol is illegal and, on top of other penalties, can lead to suspension of your license.
cards.front: Besides other penalties, what can lying about your age to get alcohol lead to?

cards.back: For motor vehicle law violations the MVA may suspend, revoke, refuse or cancel a license, and it mails a notice giving the planned action, the reason and the steps to change or stop it.
cards.front: What does the MVA's notice of an action tell you?

cards.back: In most cases you may ask for an administrative hearing to explain why the action should not happen.
cards.front: In most cases, what may you request to explain why an MVA action should not happen?

cards.back: If your license is suspended, revoked, refused or canceled you must surrender it to the MVA, and the suspension or revocation period starts when the MVA receives it.
cards.front: When does a suspension or revocation period start?

cards.back: For a driver younger than eighteen, a parent or legal guardian may ask the MVA to cancel the license.
cards.front: Who may ask the MVA to cancel the license of a driver under eighteen?

decks.module: false identification and lying about age; MVA notices, hearings and surrendering the license

cards.back: A suspension takes away your driving privilege for a time, and in some cases the MVA may grant a restricted license for set purposes such as work and school trips.
cards.front: During a suspension, what may the MVA sometimes grant?

cards.back: Revocation is more serious than suspension: you may not drive until the MVA decides you can drive safely again.
cards.front: After a revocation, when may you drive again?

cards.back: After a revocation you must wait a minimum period before asking the MVA to reinstate your license, and the MVA may say no.
cards.front: After a revocation, can the MVA deny your request to reinstate?

cards.back: Cancellation is the most serious action: your driving privilege is ended and not restored.
cards.front: What does cancellation of a license mean?

cards.back: The MVA may cancel a license that should never have been issued, or one obtained with missing or wrong application information or by fraud.
cards.front: When may the MVA cancel a license?

cards.back: A suspension is temporary and may allow a restricted license, a revocation lasts until the MVA approves reinstatement, and a cancellation is never reinstated.
cards.front: How do suspension, revocation and cancellation differ?

cards.back: A conviction or Probation before Judgment for a moving violation while holding a Provisional License can mean a driver improvement program, a suspension or revocation, or both.
cards.front: What can a moving-violation conviction or PBJ bring for a Provisional License holder?

cards.back: When such a suspension or revocation ends, the license carries an employment and education only restriction.
cards.front: After such a suspension or revocation ends, what restriction does the license carry?

cards.back: These MVA penalties come on top of any court penalties for the conviction.
cards.front: Do these MVA penalties replace court penalties?

cards.back: After each moving-violation conviction or PBJ you must start a new eighteen-month conviction-free period before you can get your license back.
cards.front: After each moving-violation conviction or PBJ, how long is the new conviction-free period?

decks.module: the conviction-free period and stacking with court penalties

cards.back: For a provisional driver under eighteen, a first moving-violation conviction or PBJ requires a driver improvement program.
cards.front: For a provisional driver under eighteen, what does a first offense require?

cards.back: A second offense for a provisional driver under eighteen brings a thirty-day suspension and then a ninety-day employment and education only restriction.
cards.front: For a provisional driver under eighteen, what does a second offense bring?

cards.back: A third offense for a provisional driver under eighteen brings a one hundred eighty-day suspension, a young-driver improvement program and a one hundred eighty-day employment and education only restriction.
cards.front: For a provisional driver under eighteen, how long is the suspension for a third offense?

cards.back: A fourth or later offense for a provisional driver under eighteen means revocation, and every licensing test must be passed again to regain the license.
cards.front: For a provisional driver under eighteen, what does a fourth offense mean?

cards.back: For a provisional driver eighteen or older, a first offense requires a driver improvement program and a second brings a thirty-day suspension.
cards.front: For a provisional driver eighteen or older, what does a second offense bring?

cards.back: A third or later offense for a provisional driver eighteen or older brings up to a one hundred eighty-day suspension or a revocation.
cards.front: For a provisional driver eighteen or older, what can a third offense bring?

cards.back: Under eighteen, a second offense is a thirty-day suspension plus a ninety-day work-and-school restriction, while eighteen or older a second offense is a thirty-day suspension alone.
cards.front: How does a second offense differ for provisional drivers under eighteen and those eighteen or older?

cards.back: Revocation comes at a fourth offense for a provisional driver under eighteen, but a third offense can already bring revocation for one who is eighteen or older.
cards.front: At which offense can revocation come for each age group?

decks.module: penalty ladder for provisional drivers under eighteen; penalty ladder for provisional drivers eighteen and older

cards.back: Misusing disability parking spaces, plates or placards can bring big fines.
cards.front: What can misusing disability parking spaces, plates or placards bring?

cards.back: You may park in a disability space only with an MVA-issued disability plate or placard and with the qualifying person in the vehicle as driver or passenger.
cards.front: When may you park in a disability space?

cards.back: Parking in front of or blocking any part of a curb cut is a violation even if you hold a disability plate or placard.
cards.front: Is blocking a curb cut allowed if you hold a disability placard?

cards.back: Parking on any part of the access aisle beside a disability space is a violation even with a plate or placard; the aisle is the space wheelchair and mobility-device users need to get in and out.
cards.front: What is the access aisle beside a disability space for?

cards.back: Using an expired placard, or a plate or placard without the disabled person present and proper identification, is a violation.
cards.front: Which of these is a disability parking violation?

cards.back: Any fraud or misrepresentation in applying for a disability plate or placard is also a violation.
cards.front: Is fraud in applying for a disability placard a violation?

cards.back: A driver caught drinking and driving will have to install a breathalyzer car lock that keeps the vehicle from starting when alcohol is detected.
cards.front: What must a driver caught drinking and driving install?
